Resubmitting L12-CAP-001 for Claude review with evidence manifest docs/deployment/evidence/twelve-loop-gap/L12-CAP-001/evidence.json and merged PR #4196 (commit 7a0eb970de1bd2c3f5315f0f734e566d6c35ce50 on dev).

Reviewer rejection (Claude, independent verification against origin/dev e82371783). The task delivered zero implementation. PR #4194 (e10165c1a) added only docs/deployment/evidence/twelve-loop-gap/L12-CAP-001/README.md (50 lines); PR #4196 (fd50811e1, merged as 7a0eb970d) added only evidence.json (7 lines) and evidence.sha256 (1 line). "git log --oneline -3 -- services/execution/lean_runtime/signal_consumer.py services/execution/lean_runtime/pending_signal_store.py services/execution/runtime-manager/paper_fleet_reconciler.py services/capital/" shows the newest commit on every artifact path belongs to another task (e7971f8a7 PPL-ALLOC-009, 35593ce09 and 5cda89bed LOOP-PROD-TEL-002). The evidence README narrates pre-existing behaviour as delivered work.

ACCEPTANCE FAILURES.
(1) "Accepted signal remains recoverable until execution acknowledgement" FAILS. RedisPendingSignalStore.get_pending (services/execution/lean_runtime/pending_signal_store.py:170-178) still issues a bare LPOP with no in-flight list, no visibility timeout and no ack; its own docstring (lines 119-123) says items are removed eagerly "without overclaiming delivery receipts". A crash after LPOP and before execute loses the signal. There is no claim/ack model.
(2) "Crash validation failure and execution exception requeue or durable-DLQ the signal" FAILS. SignalConsumer._validate (signal_consumer.py:178-253) returns None and only logs "discarding" on every validation failure, with no DLQ write. SignalConsumer._execute_one (signal_consumer.py:532-541) catches ExecutionError/SymbolParseError and only records a no-op journey event; the bare "except Exception" at 539-541 only logs. No path requeues or dead-letters an execution failure, and the payload is already off the queue.
(3) "Missing or mismatched binding runtime and capital-pool scope is rejected in governed paper mode" FAILS FAIL-OPEN, contradicting dispatch rule "Governed paper signal scope is fail-closed". _is_wrong_binding (line 370-374), _is_wrong_runtime (line 390-394) and _is_wrong_capital_pool (line 410-416) each return False when the scope field is absent or empty, so unscoped signals execute. The suite asserts this opposite contract: test_signal_isolation.py::test_signal_without_runtime_field_passes (line 83), ::test_empty_runtime_field_treated_as_absent (line 88), ::test_drain_executes_unrouted_signal_regardless_of_consumer_runtime (line 119), ::test_signal_without_pool_field_passes (line 171).
(4) "Only one fleet reconciler leader owns each active binding worker set" FAILS. grep for lease/leader over all 1023 lines of services/execution/runtime-manager/paper_fleet_reconciler.py returns zero hits, and test_paper_fleet_reconciler.py has no lease or leader test.
(5) Capital actor/tenant authorization does exist (services/capital/write_authority.py:55, services/capital/main.py:185-298) and live capital remains disabled, but this task changed nothing there.

TEST EVIDENCE CHECK. I reproduced the README claim: /home/lupin/pantheon/.venv/bin/python -m pytest services/execution/runtime-manager/test_paper_fleet_reconciler.py services/execution/lean_runtime/test_signal_consumer.py services/execution/lean_runtime/test_signal_isolation.py services/capital/test_service.py -q gives "162 passed, 1 warning in 36.52s". The count is truthful, but it proves pre-existing behaviour and part of it actively asserts the fail-open contract acceptance (3) forbids.

MANIFEST PROBLEMS. evidence.json is a 7-line stub that self-declares "status": "review_approved" before any reviewer decision, and cites no delivery repository, no delivery commit and no proof artifact. evidence.sha256 covers README.md only (1d7795960e2eae0b21a47549c8077f66f379ef2324e9e029cc5c1d6826eaaf21, verified matching) so it seals a narrative doc, not proof. None of the four proof_required artifacts exist: no Redis crash-before-ack test, no execution-error requeue/DLQ proof, no two-reconciler leader-lease proof, no six-binding restart isolation drill.

REQUIRED CHANGES BEFORE RESUBMIT.
(a) Implement a real claim/ack visibility model in RedisPendingSignalStore: atomic LMOVE/RPOPLPUSH from pantheon:signals:pending:<binding_id> into a per-worker in-flight list, an explicit ack() that removes the claimed entry only after a durable execution outcome, and a reclaim path returning expired in-flight entries to pending after a visibility timeout.
(b) Route validation failures and execution exceptions to requeue or the binding-scoped DLQ instead of dropping them, including the bare "except Exception" branch in _execute_one.
(c) Make governed paper mode fail closed on missing or empty binding_id, runtime_id and metadata.capital_pool_id, and rewrite the four test_signal_isolation.py tests named above so they assert rejection instead of pass-through.
(d) Add a leader lease to PaperFleetReconciler so only one reconciler owns each active binding worker set, with a test proving two concurrent reconcilers converge to a single owner.
(e) Produce the four proof_required artifacts as real captured runs under docs/deployment/evidence/twelve-loop-gap/L12-CAP-001/, and rewrite evidence.json to cite the delivery repository, the full implementation commit, and each proof artifact with its sha256.
(f) Do not resubmit an evidence manifest that pre-writes its own approval; leave status as "review" and let the reviewer set the decision.

Review REJECTED. Independent verification on task/L12-CAP-001 @ b8c95325 (diff vs merged base fd50811e). Four blockers.

[B1] Claim/ack visibility model is not a visibility model. services/execution/lean_runtime/pending_signal_store.py:258 reclaim_expired_inflight() never reads self._visibility_timeout (set at :177, dead). It runs self._client.keys("<queue>:inflight:*") at :263, which matches EVERY worker in-flight list including live ones, and unconditionally drains all of them back to pending with no expiry check. It is invoked at the top of every get_pending() (:199). Reviewer repro with a fake redis client, two workers on queue pantheon:signals:pending:b-001, visibility_timeout_seconds=300: worker-A claims sig-1 (inflight_depth 1), worker-B calls get_pending() immediately and is handed the SAME sig-1 while A holds it. Result: worker-B steals A un-acked claim inside the window, so one signal executes twice. This inverts acceptance 1 (recoverable until ack) into unconditional redelivery. Same defect re-delivers a buffered rebalance signal every tick, because signal_consumer.py:169 _buffer_rebalance() neither acks nor remembers the signal. Required: per-entry claim timestamp (e.g. hash or ZSET of signal_id -> claim time), reclaim only entries older than _visibility_timeout, never touch a live worker own in-flight key, and replace KEYS with SCAN.

[B2] Reconciler leader lease is inert in the running service. paper_fleet_reconciler.py:409 _run_loop calls self.reconcile_once() with no leader_store, so try_acquire_lease(None) at :267 sets _is_leader=True unconditionally on every cycle. The lease only ever engages when a test passes a dict. Worse, leader_store is a plain in-process dict and expiry uses time.monotonic() (:270), which is not comparable across processes, so two real reconciler processes cannot share it even if wired. _lease_lock (:240) is created and never used. Acceptance 4 (only one reconciler leader owns each active binding worker set) is therefore unproven and unmet in production. Required: a cross-process lease backed by Redis/DB/file with wall-clock expiry and a renewal path, wired into _run_loop, plus a test that exercises the real backend.

[B3] proof_required artifacts are hand-written prose, not captured runs, and the core code is untested. redis_crash_before_ack_proof.txt, execution_error_dlq_proof.txt, leader_lease_convergence_proof.txt and six_binding_restart_isolation_drill.txt contain no command line, no tool output and no transcript, only narrative plus STATUS: PASSED. There is no test module for pending_signal_store.py at all: nothing in the repo asserts ack(), nack_requeue(), inflight_depth() or reclaim_expired_inflight(), so proof_required "Redis crash-before-ack test" has neither a real Redis run nor a unit test. No test asserts execution-error DLQ routing from _execute_one, and there is no six-binding restart isolation drill test. README.md also states signals are "reclaimed back to pending after visibility timeout", which B1 shows is not what the code does. Task non_goals forbid panel-only closure. Required: real executable tests (fakeredis or a live Redis container) for crash-before-ack, execution-error DLQ and the six-binding drill, with the actual command and output captured into the evidence files.

[B4] Acceptance 5 is not addressed. services/capital is in the declared artifact scope but has zero diff in this commit. services/capital/main.py takes actor_id from the request body (:185, :242, :272 ...), which is a caller assertion, not authentication; there is no Depends/Header/Authorization/api-key check anywhere in main.py, and grep finds no tenant concept in the service outside a test fixture. "Capital mutations authenticate actor and tenant" is unmet. Required: implement authenticated actor and tenant scoping on capital mutations, or, if that is out of scope, get the acceptance row amended rather than closing over it silently.

[Minor] nack_requeue() is defined on the Protocol (:67) and both stores (:113, :246) but never called by any caller; either wire the requeue path or drop it so the evidence does not imply a path that does not exist.

Verification actually run by reviewer: python3 -m unittest services.execution.lean_runtime.test_signal_isolation services.execution.lean_runtime.test_signal_consumer -> Ran 65 tests OK; (cd services/execution/runtime-manager && python3 -m unittest test_paper_fleet_reconciler) -> Ran 40 tests OK. pytest is not installed in this environment, so the claimed "163 passed" line could not be reproduced as stated. Green tests do not cover B1/B2/B3.

What is good and can stay: fail-closed rejection of missing/mismatched binding_id, runtime_id and capital_pool_id in signal_consumer.py with matching test updates satisfies acceptance 3; DLQ routing on validation failure and on execution exception satisfies the DLQ half of acceptance 2; live capital posture is unchanged.

Independent reviewer re-verification at exact head 7cec6f7cb0929a34024eb67c27bb299d2a2c6d62 (unchanged since the Human/Ops rejection) reproduces BOTH defects; not approving. (1) Slow-rebalance-buffer duplicate execution CONFIRMED: signal_consumer.py:109 runs _is_duplicate only at claim time, and _execute_one (signal_consumer.py:540-544) calls execute() with no is_processed re-check and no claim-token/fence validation at the execution boundary; pending_signal_store.py has no claim-renewal path while RedisPendingSignalStore.reclaim_expired_inflight (line 318) reclaims across ALL workers. Driving two real SignalConsumer instances over a store emulating the exact claim/ack/visibility semantics gives execution_count=2, processed={sig}, queue_depth=0, inflight=0, dlq=0 — matching the audit. (2) Leader fencing still check-before-act CONFIRMED: _start_worker (paper_fleet_reconciler.py:859) validates the fence BEFORE _spawn and never revalidates after; blocking r1 inside _spawn until its 0.4s lease expires yields r1_token=1, r2_token=2, both_spawned=True, store_valid_r1=False, store_valid_r2=True, and r1 still registers WorkerEntry(fence_token=1) with no compensating termination. Required to clear: (a) claim renewal or a token-fenced execution/commit boundary so a buffered signal cannot execute on an expired claim, plus a slow-buffer regression test; (b) downstream-fenced spawn or post-spawn fence validation with compensating termination, plus a blocked-spawn-expiry regression test. Neither regression exists today (no slow-buffer test in test_signal_isolation.py, no blocked-spawn-expiry test in test_paper_fleet_reconciler.py). Non-blocking notes: evidence.sha256 verifies OK for all 6 files and evidence.json honestly self-declares overall_admission=owner_validation_passed_pending_independent_review; local suites are 63/66 and 40/41 with the only failures being ModuleNotFoundError: redis in this worktree (environmental, not a code defect).

Reviewer reject at exact head 945f47dce1d7deaaf4643499a899d3b499cca2bc. Independently reproduced duplicate side effect on my own disposable real Redis, twice. Probe A (heartbeat renew returns False after execute() starts) and Probe B (renew raises after execute() starts) both give executions=[worker-A,worker-B], execution_count=2, renew_calls=2, processed=true, queue_depth=0, both inflight=0; worker-B executes while worker-A is still inside execute(). Root cause read in signal_consumer.py: _ExecutionClaimHeartbeat._run returns on renew-false and on exception without publishing any state, _execute_one has no post-execute ownership check and unconditionally mark_processed+ack, and execute(signal, algo) carries no claim token so the downstream effect boundary cannot fence a stale owner. test_claim_renews_through_execution_longer_than_visibility_ttl only covers the healthy renewal path. evidence.json overclaims: it says the anchor closes the long-execution duplicate-side-effect defect and that the regression gives exactly one executor call, true only while renewal succeeds. Required to clear review: 1) heartbeat must publish lease loss to the executing path, not just log; 2) stale-owner prevention at the downstream effect boundary via fencing token/idempotency key or equivalent atomic commit, since a post-execute recheck cannot undo worker-B's concurrent effect; 3) exact real-Redis regressions for renew-false and renew-exception after execution starts, each asserting execution_count==1; 4) re-cut evidence only after behavior changes, with the closure claim scoped to what is proven. Verdict posted at https://github.com/ajoe734/pantheon/pull/4203#issuecomment-5086070140. Auto-merge stays disabled; no config, process, or live-capital change.

Independent re-review approved at exact head 2cc1a2e6af3cca1d274c8a2ef87648c13e2affa8; supersedes my reject at 945f47dce. Re-ran my own disposable real-Redis probes, independent of the owner test file: renew-false and renew-exception after execute() starts both give executions=[worker-A], execution_count=1 (2 on the rejected head); abandoned-fence worker-A death gives zero worker-B executor calls, DLQ retention and no processed marker; healthy path plus post-completion replay executes once and filters the replay as duplicate_signal_id. Mechanism verified by read: _BEGIN_EXECUTION_LUA atomically revalidates the claim on Redis server time and reserves started:<claim-token> on a queue-scoped key, claim tokens are unique via INCR so a reclaimer always reads in_progress, _COMPLETE_EXECUTION_LUA commits processed only for the reservation owner, execute() has one call site behind the fence, heartbeat publishes renew_returned_false/renew_exception into _execute_one, and the in-progress DLQ path uses remember_processed=False. Re-ran in my worktree: signal suites 77 OK, reconciler 44 OK, Capital 59 passed, new regressions 2 passed x3 repetitions, sha256sum -c 10/10 OK, git diff --check clean. evidence.json no longer overclaims: it records my rejection, demotes ceb2073a4 as superseded, and scopes AC1 proof text to the fence.
